description: Semantic event routing for Kafka message streams. Tags events with a fixed-size color coordinate carried in a message header, so consumers can filter on channel-routing logic without deserializing the payload.

transform.notes: RGB is used directly (not perceptually transformed) because routing decisions operate on raw channel thresholds and byte comparisons, not perceptual distance.

R.label: Urgency / Priority
R.description: High values indicate urgent or priority events requiring immediate processing.
R.interpretation: R >= 200: urgent/priority. Lower values: normal or background priority.

G.label: Success / Normal Operation
G.description: High values indicate successful or normal-path events.
G.interpretation: G >= 200 with low R/B: success or steady-state event.

B.label: Info / Analytics
B.description: High values indicate informational, analytics, or observability events.
B.interpretation: B >= 200 with low R/G: informational/analytics event.

anchors.label: Urgent / Priority
anchors.description: Time-critical events requiring immediate consumer attention
anchors.semantic_context: Alerting, incident response, priority inference requests

anchors.label: Warning
anchors.description: Degraded or at-risk conditions that are not yet critical
anchors.semantic_context: Retry exhaustion warnings, threshold breaches, elevated latency

anchors.label: Success / Normal
anchors.semantic_context: Completed transactions, healthy heartbeats, normal telemetry

anchors.label: Info / Analytics
anchors.semantic_context: Metrics, logs, usage analytics, audit trails

quality_config.notes: Routing is threshold-based rather than proximity-based; confidence reflects channel separation margin rather than perceptual distance.

confidence_factors.notes: Weighted toward anchor proximity since routing decisions are effectively nearest-anchor channel classification.

compliance_notes: Not intended for regulated domains; routing decisions here are infrastructure-level and do not require the audit guarantees used in medical or financial schemas.

target_use_cases: Multi-modal AI pipeline routing (e.g., route by modality/priority without parsing payload)
Large-payload streams where content-based routing is cost-prohibitive
Dynamic/ad-hoc routing rules defined by color-channel thresholds
not_suitable_for: Tiny payloads where deserialization cost is negligible
Cases where the routing key is already encoded in the topic name
Strict, latency-critical throughput requirements where even a fixed-size header adds unacceptable overhead
usage_guidelines.integration_notes: Carry the hex coordinate as a fixed-size Kafka message header (e.g., 'vrgb-color: #FF0000') rather than embedding it in the payload, so routing never requires payload deserialization.

routing_logic.warm_colors: R > 128 and (R > G) and (R > B): routed to urgent/priority consumers
routing_logic.cool_colors: B > 128 and (B > R) and (B > G): routed to informational/analytics consumers
routing_logic.high_priority: R >= 200: routed ahead of queued background work
routing_logic.real_time: min_confidence satisfied and R >= 150: routed to low-latency consumer group
routing_logic.batch_processing: R < 100 and G < 100 and B < 100 (grayscale-like): routed to batch/background consumers
routing_logic.custom: Arbitrary predicate over (R, G, B), e.g. red_channel(min=200) filters R >= 200 regardless of G/B

example_interpretations.action: Route to standard processing consumer group
Route to batch consumer group, process on schedule

kafka_header.description: Map VRGB coordinate to a Kafka message header for zero-deserialization routing

kafka_streams.description: Production topology: pre-filter by header color in a Kafka Streams (Java) application before fanning out to downstream, per-channel topics

mapping.topology: source topic -> branch by 'vrgb-color' header -> per-channel topics -> dedicated consumers

version_history.changes: Initial schema for Kafka semantic event routing use case (VRGB-Kafka)
